path: agy acp over standard input and output (the Agent Client Protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line)

version.how: the installed binary run with a private empty home and a minimal environment: no sign-in, no model turn
version.fixtures_recorded_with: hand-made from the ACP documentation; initialize and session/new follow what the installed program answered

session/new.not_recorded: the account tier that the answer's _meta names: it is the program's, not data of this record

client_requests.initialize: sent once at the start with protocolVersion 1 and the client capabilities above
client_requests.session/new: mapped: `[session started] model=<currentModelId>`; the sessionId is kept in the registry as the provider session
client_requests.session/resume: mapped (P04): preferred when the program advertises it, no replay; `[provider reconnected]`
client_requests.session/load: mapped (P04): used when resume is not advertised or fails; the replay it sends is not copied
client_requests.session/prompt: mapped: one text block per input; the answer's stopReason ends the turn
client_requests.session/cancel: mapped (a notification): a stopped session cancels the turn it is in

agent_requests.session/request_permission: mapped to an approval (P03): the prompt is the command or the title; allow answers the allow_once option, deny the reject_once option, and either answers cancelled when the option is not offered (never widened to an always option)

session_updates.agent_message_chunk: mapped: a fragment of text; a line is a record when it is complete, the rest when the turn or a tool call ends
session_updates.tool_call: mapped: `$ command` for an execute call with a command, otherwise `[tool] title`
session_updates.tool_call_update: mapped on completed or failed: `[tool error]` for failed, up to 20 lines of text as `> line`, up to 8 diffs as `[patch] path`
session_updates.user_message_chunk: ignored (the host records the person's inputs itself; also what a load replays)

unsupported.reason: the program does its own file and shell work in its own process, as in a terminal; only its permission requests reach the person
Lico never signs in for the person and never reads the program's credentials; the person signs in with agy itself

unsupported.feature: a model, effort or mode switch (session/set_model, session/set_mode)
unsupported.reason: out of scope for 0.9.0: the program's own default, shown in the header
